title: Full-security oblivious shuffling in worst-case logarithmic time
summary: Construct a full-domain secure oblivious shuffle whose every card trajectory uses only logarithmically many one-bit PRF calls in the worst case.

formal_statement.body: For every domain size $N$ and fixed target statistical distance $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$, construct an oblivious shuffle on $[N]$, equivalently an information-theoretic PRF-to-PRP conversion, that remains indistinguishable from a uniform permutation when the adversary queries all $q=N$ points and for which every card trajectory uses $\Theta(\log N)$ calls to a constant-output-length PRF in the worst case, or prove that no such construction exists in this model.

scope.domain: Oblivious shuffles and information-theoretic PRF-to-PRP conversions on arbitrary finite domains
assumptions: A card can be evaluated without tracking the other cards
The adversary may query all N domain points
The primitive is a constant-output-length PRF, including a one-bit-output PRF
The logarithmic evaluation bound holds for every card trajectory, not only in expectation
Security is measured at a fixed target statistical distance
parameters: worst-case number of primitive calls per card
scope.unresolved_remainder: Later work obtains logarithmic depth below the full-domain endpoint, full-domain depth $O(\log^2 N)$, sharper strict-query Swap-or-Not bounds, or worst-case logarithmically many calls to a stronger larger-domain permutation. No inspected construction simultaneously achieves $q=N$ security and worst-case $\Theta(\log N)$ total calls to a constant-output-length PRF.

provenance.note: The first archived ePrint version dated September 4, 2013 contains the explicit open question. Earlier cited shuffle results define prior bounds but do not state this complete worst-case target.

progress.summary: The first archived ePrint version asks for full-domain security together with worst-case logarithmic single-card evaluation from a constant-output-length PRF.

Switching networks achieve logarithmic depth for any fixed $(1-\varepsilon)N$ tracked elements and $O(\log^2 N)$ depth for all $N$ elements; Whitened Swap-or-Not gives logarithmic-round near-full security in a related ideal-component model.
citation_labels: Czumaj, logarithmic switching networks below full-domain security

progress.summary: Reverse cycle walking attains full-domain security with worst-case logarithmically many calls to a partially secure larger-domain cipher, but those calls are not constant-output PRF calls.
Sharper Swap-or-Not bounds and Cycle Slicer improve strict-query security and domain targeting, respectively, without reaching the complete full-domain logarithmic-call target.
The expanded Thorp-shuffle article still identifies full-domain constant-pass mixing as open and describes Sometimes-Recurse as logarithmic only in expected time.
Mix-Swap-Unmix achieves full security using one-bit Swap-or-Not components, but its logarithmic outer and inner round counts yield a quadratic-logarithmic primitive-call cost.
